routes.label: Express every score contribution using one count

question: The players on a basketball team made some three-point shots, some two-point shots, and some one-point free throws. They scored as many points with two-point shots as with three-point shots. Their number of successful free throws was one more than their number of successful two-point shots. The team’s total score was \(61\) points. How many free throws did they make?
solution:
Let \(x\) be the number of successful two-point shots. These contributed \(2x\) points. The three-point shots contributed the same number of points, so they also contributed \(2x\), even though their shot count was different. There were \(x+1\) successful free throws, each worth one point.

Adding the three contributions gives
\[
2x+2x+(x+1)=61,
\]
so \(5x=60\) and \(x=12\). Therefore the team made \(12+1=13\) free throws.

This is feasible: \(12\) two-point shots and \(8\) three-point shots each contribute \(24\) points, and \(24+24+13=61\). The answer is \(\boxed{13}\), choice A.
